name: M-Lab Starlink Connectivity Source Nodes
description: M-Lab NDT statistics pipeline -> SDS $CNP constellation-network-performance records (typed contracts 1.0: FlatBuffers only, no JSON and no base64 between modules). Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a TimerTick into ONE whole-file HttpRequest (HREQ) GET of https://statistics.measurementlab.net/v0/asn/<ASN>/<YEAR>/histogram_daily_stats.json (anonymous HTTPS, no BigQuery, no auth) whose CONTEXT is the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (INGQ) skeleton (schema, provider, source name and URL, reconcile None, archive naming), echoed by hostcap/http-request in the HttpResponse; `parse` reads that HttpResponse (HRSP), collapses the eight per-date log-bucket rows into one aggregate per UTC day and emits a size-prefixed $CNP record stream, the IngestRequest for hostcap/storage-ingest (the job completed with the batch id, licence tags and provenance) and the HttpResponse verbatim as the raw document. Starlink IS the client-ASN key: the upstream query groups by client.Network.ASNumber and AS14593 is SPACEX-STARLINK, so no constellation is ever inferred from a throughput number. A quantity exists only as a CNPMetric with UNITS and PROVENANCE, and CNPMetric has no scalar VALUE: throughput publishes six CNPStatistic entries (MINIMUM, PERCENTILE 25, MEDIAN, MEAN, PERCENTILE 75, MAXIMUM) in Mbps verbatim and minimum-RTT publishes exactly one MEDIAN in ms. REGION is omitted entirely because the per-ASN export carries no geographic key. M-Lab test data is CC0, so every metric carries LICENSE CC0-1.0, M-Lab's own citation in ATTRIBUTION and NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY false, and the batch's source tags carry LICENSE CC0-1.0 with the citation. Node CONFIG through the builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall (SDS $PIV, one ModuleConfig FlatBuffer): mlab_stats_url, mlab_stats_base_url, mlab_asn, mlab_year, mlab_http_timeout_ms, mlab_provider_id, mlab_if_none_match, mlab_if_modified_since, mlab_record_cap, mlab_max_days. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted on the parse node: the method emits a single FlowNotice (Unchanged, not-modified) on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are pure single-pass transforms over one fetched JSON table: `request` builds one HttpRequest from node CONFIG, and `parse` walks the M-Lab per-ASN statistics rows once, collapsing the eight bucket rows of each date into a single $CNP record appended to one output stream. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out and nothing for a second thread to do; the whole cost is one linear scan of a ~0.5 MB body. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Builds the M-Lab per-ASN statistics fetch from a TimerTick: ONE whole-file HttpRequest per cycle (the statistics pipeline publishes a static per-ASN-per-year artifact, not a paged API) with an identifying User-Agent, conditional-request validators from node CONFIG when set, and the parse job in CONTEXT (one size-prefixed IngestRequest). BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK) from the flow's timer trigger.

inputPorts.description: Cron timer tick (its fields are not read).

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ) for hostcap/http-request: GET the per-ASN statistics file, headers user-agent / accept (and if-none-match / if-modified-since from CONFIG), TIMEOUT_MS mlab_http_timeout_ms; CONTEXT: the parse job, one size-prefixed IngestRequest (SCHEMA CNP.fbs, TAGS PROVIDER_ID / SOURCE_NAME mlab-ndt-statistics / SOURCE_URL, RECONCILE None, ARCHIVE mlab / histogram_daily_stats.json).

methods.description: Reads the HttpResponse carrying the M-Lab per-ASN export and its job (CONTEXT), collapses the eight per-date log-bucket rows into one $CNP aggregate per UTC day (WINDOW_START inclusive, WINDOW_STOP exclusive, AGGREGATION_PERIOD DAY) and emits a size-prefixed $CNP record stream, the IngestRequest for storage-ingest and the HttpResponse verbatim for archiving. Throughput stays in Mbps and RTT in ms — units are never silently converted — and the histogram columns and geometric means are named as unencoded in the batch provenance WARNINGS rather than forced into a CNPStatistic that would mean something else. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the host presents the ETag / Last-Modified it recorded from the previous 2xx for this URL, so an unchanged export answers 304 with no body. The method then emits a single FlowNotice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced. Any other non-200 status (or a failed exchange, STATUS 0) fails closed with nothing emitted.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, the request's CONTEXT (the job, a size-prefixed IngestRequest), RETRIEVED_MS.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP response carrying the M-Lab per-ASN statistics file, its job echoed in CONTEXT.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (INGQ) for hostcap/storage-ingest: SCHEMA CNP.fbs, TAGS (PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID = sha256 of the payload, SOURCE_URL, CONTENT_KEY_ID public, SOURCE_PEER source:mlab, LICENSE CC0-1.0, LICENSE_URL, CITATION), RECONCILE from the job (None), ARCHIVE from the job, PROVENANCE (status, validators, retrieval time, parser, source / normalized SHA-256, counts, WARNINGS naming the unencoded source columns and any days dropped by mlab_max_days).
The HttpResponse (HRSP) the batch was made from, verbatim: its BODY is the M-Lab histogram_daily_stats.json storage-ingest archives under the request's ARCHIVE naming.
FlowNotice (FNTC): KIND Unchanged, SCHEMA CNP.fbs, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, REASON not-modified, ITEMS the source URL, AT_MS the host's retrieval time.

outputPorts.description: Emitted ONLY when the fetch answered HTTP 304 Not Modified (the host sent the recorded ETag / Last-Modified validators): one notice frame and no meta/records/raw frames, so the ingest node never becomes ready and nothing is stored or announced.
